scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.

actual_scope: For the PR #4067 two-window R437 carrier, derive the cancellation-free reverse row-l1 coefficient and decide whether the composed-word integer 1113998, or a shared 21-bit width cap, covers the candidate coefficient.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one precision, hosting or restoration implication. This package answers that for one published finite carrier: the reverse row coefficient rises from 1113998 to 1123650, so the old integer does not cover the candidate, while both integers still have bit length 21. It is a scoped coefficient certificate, not an all-size transfer theorem.
bottleneck_link: A moment bracket that reads only the rank profile and the bad-event surcharge can report a paid improvement while the reverse precision coefficient has increased. The selected conditional kappa stays in force until that coefficient is inside a named envelope.
stop_rule: Stop after the reverse and forward coefficients, the shared peak address, the 21-bit comparison, and the unchanged forward child count that leaves the published bad-event surcharge unchanged. Do not regenerate the pooled compiler catalogue.
evidence: Author-checked finite replay. verify.py prints PASS_R437_REVERSE_ROW_COEFFICIENT with old_reverse 1113998, new_reverse 1123650, delta 9652, forward 49347, bit_width 21, children 2915, add_delta 3, old_integer_coefficient_covers false and bit_width_cap_covers true. independent.py prints the same coefficients and peak [158, 223, 8689]. test_verify.py rejects an unchanged candidate and a duplicated peak add.
